content: 1. Fosfomycin should not be used in more than one single dose of MONUROL to treat a single episode of acute cystitis. Administering repeated daily doses of MONUROL does not enhance clinical success or microbiological eradication rates compared to single-dose therapy, but it does increase the likelihood of adverse events. 2. Urine specimens for culture and susceptibility testing should be collected both before and after completing therapy. 3. Patients should be informed that MONUROL can be taken with or without food. 4. Patients should be advised that their symptoms should improve within two to three days after taking MONUROL. If symptoms do not improve, they should contact their healthcare provider. 5. Diarrhea is a common side effect of antibiotics and usually resolves once the antibiotic is discontinued. 6. Patients should be made aware that watery and bloody stools, with or without stomach cramps and fever, can occur even two or more months after completing antibiotic treatment. If this happens, they should contact their physician immediately. 7. When co-administered with MONUROL, metoclopramide, a drug that increases gastrointestinal motility, reduces the serum concentration and urinary excretion of fosfomycin. Other drugs that enhance gastrointestinal motility may have similar effects. 8. Cimetidine does not affect the pharmacokinetics of fosfomycin when co-administered with MONUROL. 9. Long-term carcinogenicity studies in rodents have not been conducted because MONUROL is intended for single-dose treatment in humans. 10. MONUROL has not shown mutagenic or genotoxic effects in in vitro tests (Ames bacterial reversion test, cultured human lymphocytes, Chinese hamster V79 cells) or in the in vivo mouse micronucleus assay. 11. MONUROL did not impair fertility or reproductive performance in male and female rats. 12. Fosfomycin crosses the placental barrier when administered intramuscularly as the sodium salt at doses equivalent to four times the human dose based on body weight and seven times the human dose based on mg/m². Fetotoxicities were observed at maternally toxic doses, likely due to the sensitivity of rabbits to changes in intestinal microflora caused by antibiotic administration. 13. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Because animal reproduction studies are not always predictive of human response, MONUROL should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. 14. It is unknown whether fosfomycin tromethamine is excreted in human milk. Since many drugs are excreted in human milk and due to the potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants, a decision should be made to either discontinue nursing or not administer the drug, considering the importance of the drug to the mother. 15. The safety and effectiveness of MONUROL in children aged 12 years and under have not been established in adequate and well-controlled studies. 16. Clinical studies of MONUROL did not include sufficient numbers of subjects aged 65 and older to determine whether they respond differently from younger subjects. 17. Other reported clinical experience has not identified differences in responses between elderly and younger patients. 18. In general, dose selection for elderly patients should be cautious, typically starting at the lower end of the dosing range, reflecting the greater frequency of decreased hepatic, renal, or cardiac function, and the presence of concomitant disease or other drug therapy.
